qs.q: In SMC, what does "smart money" mean?
o: The big players: banks, funds, large institutions and market makers
Retail traders who are always in profit
Groups that sell signals
Central banks only
qs.e: Smart money is the big players whose orders are too large to be filled at a single price.

qs.q: Why does a big player need many orders on the opposite side to build a position?
o: Its order is too large to be filled at a single price
The broker forces it to, so it can earn more spread
It only trades at night when the market is quiet
It has little capital, so it borrows orders from others
qs.e: Filling a huge order needs plenty of opposite orders, which is why price often goes first to where orders sit.

qs.q: What is the core idea of SMC?
o: Price often visits the order pools first, then moves its real way
Price always moves in a straight line toward its target
You should buy at every support without thinking
No trade is possible without at least one indicator
qs.e: Places full of stops and orders are liquidity; price often takes them before its real move.

qs.q: Classic price action says "buy at support". How does SMC look at that same support?
o: It treats the stop losses under support as liquidity
It ignores support completely
It always sells there
It treats support as a guarantee
qs.e: In SMC the stops below support are SSL, which price often comes to take.

qs.q: What is the correct order of the five parts of SMC?
o: Structure, liquidity, POI, time, entry
Entry, time, POI, liquidity, structure
POI, entry, structure, time, liquidity
Liquidity, entry, structure, POI, time
qs.e: Trend first (structure), then where the orders are (liquidity), then the zone (POI), then time, and finally the entry.

qs.q: Why should you not break the order of this course?
o: Each part rests on the one before, so skipping misreads the next
The last lessons are hard, so they should be read first
The website does not allow lessons out of order
Order makes no difference; start anywhere you like
qs.e: Each part stands on the one before it, so jumping to order blocks without the basics is a mistake.

qs.q: Where do most SMC concepts like order blocks, FVGs and killzones come from?
o: The work of ICT, the Inner Circle Trader
Books on Elliott Wave theory
The RSI and MACD indicators
An old book on Fibonacci ratios
qs.e: These ideas come from ICT and were later taught by others under their own names, so definitions differ slightly.

qs.q: What is a typical win rate for SMC setups?
o: About 35 to 50 percent
More than 90 percent
Always 100 percent
Under 10 percent
qs.e: SMC gives a small SL and large RR, but the win rate is often 35 to 50 percent, so risk management is essential.

qs.q: Which statement about SMC is true?
o: It is a language of probabilities, not guarantees
Every order block works
Every sweep is followed by a reversal
No backtesting is needed
qs.e: Explaining moves after the fact is easy; predicting them is hard. That is why backtesting is essential.

qs.q: The trend is making HH and HL. What kind of trade does an SMC trader look for?
o: Buys only
Sells only
Both equally
No trades at all
qs.e: HH and HL is an uptrend, so the bias is bullish and only buy setups are considered.

qs.q: In the uptrend example, when was the entry taken?
o: SSL was swept into the POI and a lower-timeframe CHoCH formed
As soon as the first green candle printed, at market
When RSI dropped below 30 and showed oversold
Any time at all, as long as the higher trend is up
qs.e: Sweep, POI and a lower-timeframe CHoCH together make the entry; the stop goes below the sweep wick.

qs.q: What is at the end of every phase in this course?
o: A gate: move on only when its conditions are met
A paid exam
Nothing
A link to open a live account
qs.e: Each phase gate lists what you must be able to do before moving on.

t: Candlestick Anatomy: Body, Wick and Momentum

qs.q: What are the four numbers of a candle?
o: Open, high, low, close
Buy, sell, SL, TP
Spread, lot, pip, margin
Volume, RSI, MACD, EMA
qs.e: Every candle is made of just four numbers: OHLC.

qs.q: What does a candle's body tell you?
o: Whose pressure won in the end
Where price went but was not accepted
The colour of the next candle
How big the spread is
qs.e: The body shows the decision; a big body means a strong decision in one direction.

qs.q: What does a long upper wick mean?
o: Selling came in above; price was not accepted there
Buyers are very strong and price will go higher
The next candle will surely be big and green
Wicks mean nothing; only the body matters
qs.e: A wick shows price went there but was not accepted; an upper wick shows selling from above.

qs.q: When a wick crosses a level but the body closes back inside, what is it often in SMC?
o: A sweep
A BOS
A confirmed breakout
Trend continuation
qs.e: Wick beyond, body back inside = sweep; body closing beyond = break.

qs.q: How do you recognise a momentum candle?
o: Body at least 70%, small wicks
Body under 30%, wicks on both sides
Long wicks both sides, small body
Always green, any size at all
qs.e: A momentum candle is a fast decision by one side; in SMC it is called displacement.

qs.q: Gold M15 candle: open 4,128.40, high 4,135.90, low 4,127.10, close 4,134.80. What kind is it?
o: A bullish momentum candle
A bearish rejection candle
An indecision (doji) candle
A bearish momentum candle
qs.e: Body 6.4 and range 8.8 dollars, about 73%; the close is above the open, so it is bullish.

qs.q: If the body is below 30% of the full range, what is the candle?
o: An indecision or rejection candle
A strong momentum candle
An ordinary normal candle
A BOS breakout candle
qs.e: A body under 30% means no decision, or one side's price was rejected.

qs.q: When should you treat a candle as a rejection?
o: One wick twice the body or more
The body is over 70% of the range
Whenever the candle is red
When the candle has no wicks
qs.e: If one wick is twice the body or longer, price was not accepted there.

qs.q: How do impulse candles differ from pullback candles?
o: Impulses: big bodies; pullbacks: small, overlapping candles
Both have exactly the same kind of candles
Pullbacks: big bodies; impulses: small candles
Impulses have only long wicks and almost no body
qs.e: If big momentum candles suddenly appear inside a pullback, the trend may be changing.

qs.q: When should you decide on a BOS, CHoCH or sweep?
o: After the candle closes
Quickly, while the candle is forming
The next day
Only during news
qs.e: A forming candle can give everything back in its last minutes, so decide on the close.

qs.q: How many M15 candles make one H1 candle, and what is a long H1 wick often on M15?
o: Four; price went and came back (a full move)
Two; nothing special happens on M15
Eight; one long trend on M15
Four; an empty price gap on M15
qs.e: A higher-timeframe wick is often a complete sweep and reversal on the lower timeframe.

qs.q: "Green means buy, red means sell." Why is this wrong?
o: Location, size and close matter more than colour
It is completely correct and enough
Because brokers can change the colours
Because only the wick length matters
qs.e: A red candle with a big lower wick at support can be a bullish sign.

t: Swing High and Swing Low: How to Mark Swings

qs.q: What is a swing high?
o: Its high is above both neighbours
It has the biggest body
The very first candle of the day
Any green closed candle
qs.e: A swing high is the peak of a wave; a swing low is its trough.

qs.q: What does the two-candle rule say?
o: At least two lower-high candles on each side
Enter a trade after two candles form
Mark one swing after every two candles
Mark only two swings on the chart
qs.e: At least two lower-high candles on each side confirm a swing high; the opposite for a swing low.

qs.q: Why should you not treat the latest "swing" on a live chart as final?
o: Until two candles form on its right, it is only a possible swing
Because the last swing is always wrong
Because the broker changes it
It is fine to treat it as final
qs.e: A swing is always confirmed later.

qs.q: What is the difference between a major and a minor swing?
o: A major is followed by a big move; a minor sits inside a wave
They are the same; only the names differ
The minor sets the bias; the major is for entries
Majors form only on M1; minors only on Daily
qs.e: Major swings are for bias, BOS and CHoCH; minor swings for entries and internal structure.

qs.q: Where do you take the level of a swing high or low from?
o: The tip of the wick
The body close
The middle of the body
The open price
qs.e: Price really reached the wick, and that is where stops and liquidity sit.

qs.q: What decides whether a swing has been broken?
o: A body close
A wick
The candle colour
An indicator
qs.e: The level comes from the wick; the break decision from the body close.

qs.q: About how many candles should be on the chart when marking swings?
o: Between 50 and 150
Only 5
More than 1,000
Only the last candle
qs.e: With too many candles the eye gets lost; the lesson uses 50 to 80 and 100 to 150.

qs.q: If two swing highs appear with no low between them, what do you do?
o: Keep only the higher one
Keep both
Remove both
Keep the lower one
qs.e: Swing highs and swing lows alternate.

qs.q: How many important swings does a good H1 chart usually have in a day?
o: Only 2 to 4
More than 20
Every candle is a swing
None
qs.e: The aim is to see the chart's story, not count every wiggle.

qs.q: Gold H1 rises from 4,112 to 4,131.50, pulls back to 4,121.80, then rises to 4,140.20. What is the structure?
o: HH and HL, an uptrend
LH and LL, a downtrend
A range
Nothing can be said
qs.e: 4,140.20 is above the previous high 4,131.50 (HH), and 4,121.80 is above the earlier low 4,112 (HL).

qs.q: In a range, swing highs and lows form at equal levels. What do they become later?
o: A key part of liquidity
Strong order blocks
FVGs waiting to fill
Useless old levels
qs.e: Equal highs and lows of a range are a key part of liquidity in Phase 2; don't trade the middle of a range.

qs.q: Which timeframe is used for the bias (direction)?
o: Daily and H4 (Weekly if needed)
M1 and M5
M15 only
Any, it makes no difference
qs.e: The higher timeframe gives the bias, the middle one the zones, the lower one the entry.

qs.q: What is a simple timeframe combination for beginners?
o: H4 for bias, H1 for zones, M15 for entries
M1 for bias, M5 for zones, H4 for entries
M1 only
Daily for entries, M1 for bias
qs.e: Start with H4/H1/M15; add M5 and M1 later if needed.

qs.q: What is the maximum risk on one trade?
o: 1% (0.5% at first)
5% (for faster growth)
10% (on a small account)
Always 2% to 3%
qs.e: At 1%, even 10 losses cost about 10% of the account, not all of it.

qs.q: What is the correct order for the lot and the SL?
o: SL from structure, then distance, then lot
Lot first, then fit the SL to it
Target first, then SL, lot by feel
Lot from 10% of balance, then the SL
qs.e: Fixing the lot first and squeezing the SL is the biggest mistake.

qs.q: What is the lot formula on Gold?
o: Risk ÷ (SL distance × 100)
Balance ÷ (SL distance × 100)
(Risk × SL distance) ÷ 100
Risk ÷ (SL distance × 10)
qs.e: On Gold 1 lot is 100 ounces, so a 1-dollar move is 100 dollars on 1 lot.

qs.q: 1,000-dollar account, 1% risk, Gold SL distance 2.5 dollars. What is the lot?
EURUSD, 1,000-dollar account, 10-dollar risk, 20-pip SL. What is the lot?
qs.e: On EURUSD 1 pip on 1 lot is about 10 dollars: 10 ÷ (20 × 10) = 0.05.

qs.q: Why should the SL on Gold not sit exactly at the edge of the zone or wick?
o: Because of the spread; leave about 0.3 to 0.5 dollars
Because the SL must always be very far
Because the broker forbids it
The edge is the best place
qs.e: The spread is charged too and widens during news, so leave some room.

qs.q: What is the daily limit?
o: Stop for the day after two losses or 2%
Up to 10 losses a day is fine
No limit
Double the lot after a loss
qs.e: Lose more than 5% in a week and spend the rest of the week only backtesting.

qs.q: Where should the stop loss go?
o: Where price reaching it proves your idea wrong
Where you can afford to lose
Always at 10 pips
Right next to the entry
qs.e: Below the last important swing low or POI for buys, above for sells, with a little room.

qs.q: At 1:2 RR, roughly what win rate do you need to break even?
o: About 34%
About 50%
About 75%
About 90%
qs.e: 50% at 1:1, about 34% at 1:2, 25% at 1:3; that is why the course uses at least 1:2.

qs.q: After 10 straight losses at 5% risk on a 1,000-dollar account, what gain do you need to get back?
o: About 67%
About 11%
About 22%
qs.e: At 5% about 599 dollars remain after 10 losses; at 1% you need only about 11%.

qs.q: 500-dollar account, 5-dollar risk, 4-dollar Gold SL. The formula gives 0.0125. Which lot do you use?
qs.e: Always round the lot down; at 0.01 the real risk is 4 dollars, or 0.8%.

qs.q: What about doubling the lot after a loss to win it back?
o: The biggest reason accounts blow up
A good way to recover losses quickly
A common method of professional traders
Safe on Gold, risky only on others
qs.e: Raising the lot after a loss is the most common way accounts are blown quickly.

t: Market Structure: HH, HL, LH, LL

qs.q: What does HL (Higher Low) mean?
o: The new low is above the previous low
The new high is above the previous high
The new low is below the previous low
The new high is below the previous high
qs.e: Each swing is named by comparing it with the previous swing of the same kind.

qs.q: What identifies a downtrend?
o: LH and LL
HH and HL
Red candles only
HH and LL
qs.e: When both highs and lows are falling, it is a downtrend.

qs.q: What is the biggest mistake in a range?
o: Entering in the middle of the range
Marking the range edges
Waiting for a breakout
Writing down the high and low
qs.e: Both edges of a range are liquidity in SMC; entering in the middle makes no sense.

qs.q: What do you use to decide the trend?
o: The last two highs and the last two lows
The colour of the last three candles
Only the last candle
The RSI value
qs.e: The trend comes from swings, not candle colours.

qs.q: Price makes an HH but also an LL. What is this?
o: Expansion; the trend is unclear
A strong uptrend; buy it
A strong downtrend; sell it
A triangle; wait for a breakout
qs.e: HH with LL is expansion; LH with HL is contraction (a triangle).

qs.q: An uptrend prints its first LH. Has the trend changed?
o: Not yet; the last HL must break on a body
Yes, the first LH ends the trend
Yes, sell now with the SL at the high
An LH means nothing in structure
qs.e: Even an uptrend sometimes prints a slightly lower high; selling the first LH is a mistake.

qs.q: Gold H1 lows: 4,108, 4,117, 4,129; highs: 4,126, 4,139, 4,147. How long does the bias stay bullish?
o: As long as price does not close below 4,129
As long as price stays above 4,147
As long as price stays above 4,108
Only for today
qs.e: The last HL is 4,129; a body close below it would be the first big sign of a trend change.

qs.q: Which three lines should you write before trading each day?
o: D1/H4 structure, the last important level, and the price at which the bias changes
How much to make today, which pair, how many trades
News list, spread, leverage
Nothing needs writing
qs.e: Knowing in advance at which price your view changes protects you from emotional decisions.

qs.q: Three red candles appear in an uptrend. What does it mean?
o: Maybe a normal pullback; swings decide
The trend has changed to a downtrend
Sell now; the reversal has started
The market has moved into a range
qs.e: Candle colour does not change the trend; the last HL must break.

qs.q: What is a BOS?
o: A structure break in the direction of the current trend
The first break against the trend
A wick touching any level
The gap between two candles
qs.e: In a bullish BOS the previous HH breaks; in a bearish BOS the previous LL.

qs.q: What is the key condition for a BOS?
o: A candle body closes beyond the level
A wick touches the level
The candle is green
Volume is high
qs.e: If only the wick went beyond and the body closed back inside, it is not a BOS; it is often a sweep.

qs.q: The last HH is 4,152.40. In London a candle reaches 4,156.10 but closes at 4,150.80. What is it?
o: Not a BOS, only a wick
A bullish BOS
A bearish CHoCH
An FVG
qs.e: The body closed below the high, so the higher price was not accepted.

qs.q: How do you draw a BOS line?
o: From the broken swing to the closing candle, with the timeframe
One long line from the chart's start to its end
A separate line on every high, with no label
Only a small mark at the wick tip
qs.e: An M15 BOS and an H4 BOS are not the same, so write the timeframe.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a benefit of a BOS?
o: It guarantees the next candle goes up
Confirming the bias
Finding POIs at the origin of the BOS move
Identifying the protected low
qs.e: A BOS confirms the trend is alive; it guarantees nothing about the next candle.

qs.q: Why do traders who jump on the first pullback after a BOS often get trapped?
o: They fall into the IDM trap
Because a BOS is always fake
Because the pullback never comes
Because the spread is high
qs.e: The first small pullback after a BOS is often inducement (lesson 1.6).

qs.q: Which is a sign of a strong BOS?
o: A big momentum candle with an FVG, closing well past the high
Small candles creeping slowly past the high
A break made in the quiet Asian hours
A break against the higher timeframe bias
qs.e: The origin of a strong BOS (order block or FVG) makes a good POI.

qs.q: After a BOS, which is the new important low?
o: The low where the BOS move began
The high of the BOS candle
The oldest low on the chart
Any small low
qs.e: In the Gold example the BOS move began at 4,144.50, so that is the new important low.

qs.q: Why is chasing the BOS candle wrong?
o: A BOS says the trend is alive; enter on a POI pullback
A reversal always follows a BOS straight away
A BOS only forms on M1, so it is useless
It is the right method; waiting costs money
qs.e: Chasing the BOS candle makes the SL large and the RR poor.

qs.q: What is a CHoCH?
o: The first structure break against the trend
A break in the trend's direction
A wick touching a level
The first candle of the day
qs.e: In a bearish CHoCH the last HL of an uptrend breaks on a body close.

qs.q: In an uptrend, at which level is a CHoCH marked?
o: At the last HL
At the highest high
At any small low
At the trend's first low
qs.e: Every HL is a floor built by buyers; when the last one breaks, the trend's character changes.

qs.q: Which is more reliable, a BOS or a CHoCH?
o: A BOS; a CHoCH needs confirmation
A CHoCH; a BOS needs confirmation
They are equal
Neither
qs.e: A BOS is with the trend; a CHoCH against it is only a first warning.

qs.q: Which is NOT one of the three ways to confirm a CHoCH?
o: The candle colour changing
The first BOS in the new direction
Displacement with an FVG
Higher timeframe agreement
qs.e: Confirmation comes from a BOS, displacement or the higher timeframe, not colour.

qs.q: In this course, what does MSS mean?
o: A lower-timeframe CHoCH made with displacement
A BOS made on the higher timeframe
A type of momentum indicator
The time the market closes
qs.e: MSS means Market Structure Shift; the Phase 5 entry models use it.

qs.q: What is the most useful idea in SMC entries?
o: HTF direction + LTF CHoCH
A reverse trade on every CHoCH
M1 signals only
Instant entry on every BOS
qs.e: The higher timeframe gives the direction; the lower-timeframe CHoCH gives the timing.

qs.q: Why is taking the reverse trade the moment a CHoCH appears wrong?
o: A CHoCH is only a warning; the old trend often resumes
A CHoCH is never right, so ignore it
A CHoCH forms from wicks only, never bodies
It isn't wrong; an instant reverse trade is right
qs.e: Pause, check the timeframe and location, and wait for confirmation and a pullback.

qs.q: Does an M5 CHoCH change an H4 trend?
o: No
Yes, always
Only in London
Only on Fridays
qs.e: Do not change the higher timeframe bias because of a lower timeframe CHoCH.

qs.q: Which CHoCH is more reliable?
o: After a sweep, inside an HTF POI, in a killzone
Mid-range, without any sweep
In Asia, slowly from small candles
In a news spike, with a big wick
qs.e: A sweep, a POI, momentum and a killzone together make a CHoCH stronger.

qs.q: M15 downtrend: 4,146 (LH), 4,128 (LL), 4,137 (LH), 4,121 (LL). Price drops to 4,118 then closes at 4,139.40. What is it?
o: A bullish CHoCH
A bearish BOS
Only a wick, nothing
Inducement (IDM)
qs.e: The Asian low was swept first, then the last LH broke on a body close. Stop below the sweep low at 4,117.

qs.q: What is swing structure used for?
o: Bias and trend
Entry timing only
Measuring spread
Calculating the lot
qs.e: Swing (major) structure gives the bias; internal (minor) structure gives entry timing and the end of pullbacks.

qs.q: LHs and LLs form inside an uptrend pullback. What is this?
o: Internal structure; the bigger trend is still up
The trend changed; it is now a downtrend
A swing CHoCH; switch the bias bearish
A range; trade both directions
qs.e: As long as the swing HL holds, the bigger trend is up.

qs.q: What simple question tells you whether a swing is internal?
o: Would its break change the bigger trend?
Is the candle at this swing red?
Did this swing form on the M1 chart?
Is the volume low at this moment?
qs.e: A swing whose break does not change the bigger trend is internal.

qs.q: How are internal structure labels written?
o: With i-, in a lighter colour and thin line
Exactly like the big swing labels
With numbers only, no letters
No labels needed; keep it in mind
qs.e: Thick lines and big labels for swing; thin or dashed lines with i- for internal.

qs.q: H1 made a BOS down, the trader sold, but price rose from the swing HL. What was the mistake?
o: It was an internal BOS in a pullback; take bias from swings
Sold too late; should have sold the first candle
The lot was too small; a bigger one would have held
No mistake at all, just bad luck
qs.e: For every BOS and CHoCH, ask which level it belongs to.

qs.q: What is the most useful job of internal structure?
o: The last i-LH breaking shows the pullback is ending
Flipping the big bias on any internal BOS
Giving a new trade signal on every candle
Only finding the edges of ranges
qs.e: An i-CHoCH at a POI or in discount is the entry trigger.

qs.q: Should you enter on every i-CHoCH?
o: No, only those at a POI or in discount
Yes, every i-CHoCH is a good entry
Only i-CHoCHs that form at night
Only sell ones, never buy ones
qs.e: An i-CHoCH without a zone is a signal in mid-air.

qs.q: Gold: H1 uptrend, swing HL 4,131. On M15 the i-LL at 4,143 breaks. What is the swing trend?
o: Still up, because 4,131 holds
Down, because the i-LL broke
A range
It cannot be known
qs.e: Selling an internal LL as if it were a swing CHoCH is a mistake.

qs.q: When does the bias change?
o: Only with a swing CHoCH
On every internal BOS
On every red candle
Every hour
qs.e: Changing bias on an internal BOS is a common mistake.

qs.q: In an uptrend, which is the protected low?
o: The low where the BOS move started
The lowest low visible on the chart
The low of the last closed candle
The lowest point of any pullback
qs.e: Buyers are defending that place; in a downtrend the reverse: the protected high.

qs.q: If the protected low breaks on a body close, what is it?
o: A CHoCH
A BOS
IDM
An FVG
qs.e: The protected low is the uptrend's last wall; when it breaks the bias turns neutral, then bearish after confirmation.

qs.q: When does the protected low move up?
o: After each new BOS, to that move's start
Every morning at the Asian open
Whenever a red candle closes
Never; marking it once is enough
qs.e: After a new BOS the old protected low is just an old level.

qs.q: What is the valid pullback rule (in an uptrend)?
o: The pullback candle takes the prior low
Three red candles form in a row
The pullback reaches 50% of the move
RSI falls below 30
qs.e: This stops every small pause being treated as a swing; only places where some liquidity was taken count.

qs.q: Two or three candles pause sideways but no low breaks. What do you do?
o: Not a valid pullback; mark no swing
Mark a new HL; the pullback is done
Buy now; the trend is continuing
Mark a CHoCH; the trend is turning
qs.e: A valid pullback needs the previous candle's low to be taken.

qs.q: Where is the most logical SL for a swing trade?
o: Below the protected low, with room
Just under the entry, 1 dollar away
Below the oldest low on the chart
No SL needed; the trend is up
qs.e: If the protected low breaks, the buy idea is wrong.

qs.q: The protected low is very far and the RR doesn't work. What do you do?
o: Use an LTF entry, or skip
Move the SL closer for no reason
Raise the lot to fix the RR
Remove the SL and take it
qs.e: For intraday trades the SL goes below the lower timeframe's protected low.

qs.q: Gold H1: a BOS move from 4,121, a pullback to 4,133, then a new BOS above 4,149. What is the protected low now?
qs.e: The new BOS move started at 4,133, so the line moves there.

qs.q: A small wick goes below the protected low but the body closes above. Has it broken?
o: No; the body-close rule applies here too
Yes, a wick is enough; sell now
Yes, the trend is over; flip the bias
Only on M1, not on H1
qs.e: Treating a wick sweep as a break is a mistake.

qs.q: What is IDM (inducement)?
o: The first small pullback after a BOS that lures early entries
The trend's very last and highest high
An indicator that shows stop hunts
The quiet time before big news
qs.e: The stops placed under that small low become liquidity.

qs.q: What does price often do with the IDM?
o: Sweeps the IDM, then moves from the real POI
Leaves straight up from the IDM, never back
Never touches the IDM, stays far away
Builds a long range at the IDM and stalls
qs.e: That is why a POI is stronger once the IDM has been swept.

qs.q: Why does IDM work?
o: Early buyers' stops become sells that fill the big buyer
The broker deliberately hunts retail stops
It is a written law of the market
It doesn't work; it is pure chance
qs.e: The stops of buyers being stopped out are sell orders.

qs.q: The IDM has not been swept and price is at a small zone above it. What do you do?
o: Avoid it, or use half risk
Buy at once with full risk
Sell at once; the zone will fail
Remove the SL and wait
qs.e: An entry before the IDM is higher risk.

qs.q: The IDM is swept and price reaches the POI. What now?
o: Wait for an LTF CHoCH, then enter
Enter at once with no confirmation
Skip it; the chance is gone
Sell instead; the zone failed
qs.e: Entering the moment the IDM is swept, without confirmation, is also a mistake.

qs.q: Which low is the IDM?
o: The first clear internal pullback after the BOS
Every small low that forms on the chart
The lowest low of the range
The trend's protected low
qs.e: Calling every small low an IDM is a mistake.

qs.q: Bearish example: BOS at 4,138, first pullback to 4,141 (IDM), POI 4,155 to 4,160. Where and when to sell?
o: After the IDM sweep, POI arrival and an M15 bearish CHoCH, near 4,153
Right away at 4,141, at the IDM itself
At market the moment 4,138 breaks
On a break above 4,160, without confirmation
qs.e: Price first reached 4,143 (taking IDM stops), then 4,156 in the POI; stop 4,163, target 4,131.

qs.q: If the IDM is not swept and price makes a new high?
o: Let it go; wait for the next BOS and IDM
Buy at once; the trend is very strong
Sell; price will surely come back
Chase it with a double lot
qs.e: In a strong trend price can leave without touching the IDM; note in your journal how often it happens.

qs.q: How does an up-wave pullback in an H4 downtrend look on M15?
o: An uptrend with HHs and HLs
A downtrend
One candle
Nothing is visible
qs.e: Every higher timeframe wave is a complete trend on a lower timeframe.

qs.q: What is the core multi-timeframe rule?
o: Trade in the HTF direction; enter on the LTF CHoCH
Trade the LTF direction; enter on the HTF
Use one timeframe only
A separate trade on every timeframe
qs.e: This gives a small SL (beyond the LTF swing) and a large target (HTF liquidity).

qs.q: Which timeframe set is for an intraday trader?
o: H4 bias, H1 zone, M15 or M5 entry
Daily bias, H4 zone, H1 entry
H1 bias, M15 zone, M1 entry
M1 only
qs.e: Daily/H4/H1 is for swing traders; H1/M15/M1 for scalpers.

qs.q: Why not open more than three timeframes?
o: Some timeframe always disagrees and you never decide
More timeframes slow the chart and crash the platform
The broker forbids more than three timeframes
More is better; you see every angle
qs.e: Three are enough: bias, zone, entry.

qs.q: The HTF is bullish and the LTF bearish (a pullback). What do you do?
o: Wait at the zone for a bullish LTF CHoCH
The LTF is bearish, so sell now
The HTF is bullish, so buy now
They disagree, so stop trading
qs.e: Enter when the LTF pullback ends in the HTF direction.

qs.q: The HTF is in a range. What is the decision?
o: No trade, or edges only
Trade every LTF signal
Buy in the middle
Sell in the middle
qs.e: There are no trades in the middle of a range.

qs.q: What do the H1 zone and the M5 CHoCH each tell you?
o: H1 says where, M5 says when
M5 says where, H1 says when
Both only give the trend direction
Both only give the SL location
qs.e: A zone alone (it can break) or a CHoCH alone (mid-air) is not enough; together they make a setup.

qs.q: In the 15-minute daily routine, when is the alert set?
o: After marking the H1 POI
First thing, before D1
After the trade closes
Only at news time
qs.e: Order: D1, H4, H1 (POI), alert, then a CHoCH on M15/M5 when the alert fires.

qs.q: What about switching timeframes to manage a trade?
o: Wrong; manage on the plan's timeframe
Right; a smaller timeframe shows more
Required; manage every trade on M1
Fine to switch only during news
qs.e: Switching timeframes makes every small wiggle look scary.

qs.q: Gold: H4 bullish, H1 POI 4,112 to 4,118, the M5 LH at 4,117 breaks. What is the trade?
o: Sell 4,117, SL 4,121, target 4,104
No trade; H4 and M5 disagree
qs.e: Both the zone (where) and the M5 CHoCH (when) are present; the target sits just before the previous H1 high at 4,138.

qs.q: In SMC, what does liquidity mean?
o: Where many stop losses and pending orders rest
The total money in the broker's account
The tallest bar on a volume indicator
The time just before the market closes
qs.e: Most traders put stops at the same kind of levels, so these places are visible on the chart.

qs.q: Where is BSL?
o: Above highs
Below lows
In the middle of a range
Only at round numbers
qs.e: Sellers' stops and breakout buy stops sit above highs and become buy orders when triggered.

qs.q: When the orders at SSL are triggered, what do they become?
o: Sell orders
Buy orders
Nothing
Pending limit orders
qs.e: Easy rule: BSL orders become buys, SSL orders become sells.

qs.q: Where does a big buyer prefer to buy?
o: Near SSL
Near BSL
Mid-range
Anywhere
qs.e: To buy it needs sellers, and long traders' stops below lows become sell orders.

qs.q: Which of these is NOT a place where liquidity builds?
o: The empty middle of a range
Equal highs or lows (EQH/EQL)
Previous day high and low
Round numbers like 4,100.00
qs.e: Rule: the more traders can see a level, the more liquidity sits behind it.

qs.q: What are the three ways an SMC trader uses liquidity?
o: Target, entry clue, and protecting his own stop
Only as a target, nothing else
Hunting other people's stops and running grids
Raising lots, hedging and recovery
qs.e: After a sweep, a lower timeframe CHoCH is the entry signal.

qs.q: Why not place your stop right under an obvious low?
o: That is where the sweep comes first
Because the broker forbids it
Because stops always go above
It is the best place
qs.e: Place it where price reaching it really proves you wrong: behind structure, with room.

qs.q: Gold H1 has ranged between 4,120 and 4,150 for two days. H4 is bullish. What is price's likely path?
o: SSL below 4,120 first, then the BSL at 4,150
A straight drop to 4,100 and a new downtrend
Above 4,150 first, then a sell setup at 4,150
Sitting at mid-range 4,135 for a long time
qs.e: The sweep under 4,120 is the buying chance and the area near 4,150 is the target.

qs.q: Which idea about liquidity is wrong?
o: The market is robbing us; it is a conspiracy
It is how large orders get filled
It is both a target and a sweep zone
Higher timeframe levels matter more
qs.e: Liquidity is not a conspiracy; it is simply how big orders are filled.

qs.q: What is an EQH?
o: Two or more highs at almost the same price
One very big candle
The highest high of the day
A trendline break
qs.e: Classic price action calls it a double top or strong resistance.

qs.q: Why does liquidity grow with every touch?
o: Each touch, more traders see it and stops pile up
Each touch lowers volume, so orders increase
As the level weakens the broker adds orders
It doesn't grow; each touch uses it up
qs.e: By the third touch breakout traders add buy stops too.

qs.q: What do traders say about a very clean double top?
o: It often breaks first and only then works
It always works without breaking
It never works
It forms only on Daily
qs.e: The buy orders above fire and fill the big seller, then price comes back down.

qs.q: On Gold H1, how much difference between two highs still counts as equal?
o: About 1 to 2 dollars
10 dollars
Exactly zero
It must be under 50 cents
qs.e: The real question: would an ordinary trader see it as one clear level? 3 to 4 dollars on H4, up to 0.5 on M5.

qs.q: A trendline breaks but structure (the protected low) holds. What is it usually?
o: A liquidity sweep
The end of the trend
A BOS
An FVG
qs.e: An SMC trader watches structure, not the line.

qs.q: Retail sells the double top. What does an SMC trader do?
o: A sweep above the top, then a bearish LTF CHoCH
Sell right there, stop just above the top
Treat it as a breakout and buy at once
Ignore the double top and trade the range
qs.e: No entry after a sweep without a lower timeframe CHoCH.

qs.q: In a bullish bias, what are EQL and trendlines below?
o: Sweep chances for buys
Downside targets for sells
Useless levels with no role
Places for a bearish BOS
qs.e: In a bullish bias liquidity below is a sweep zone and EQH above is a target.

qs.q: Why is treating every EQH as an instant sell signal wrong?
o: EQH is a target; price often goes there first
Because EQH is always a buy signal
Because EQH is only on M1
It is not wrong
qs.e: Selling below it usually means trading against the target.

qs.q: Gold M15 highs 4,138.50, 4,139.20, 4,138.80; H1 bearish. Price hits 4,142.30, closes 4,137.90, then an M5 bearish CHoCH. Where is the stop?
o: 4,143.50 (above the wick)
4,139.20 (at the high)
No stop needed
qs.e: Sell near 4,138.00, stop above the wick, target the SSL at 4,126.00; about 1:2.

qs.q: What are PDH and PDL?
o: Previous day high and low
Previous week high and low
The Asian session high and low
The protected high and low
qs.e: Almost every intraday trader watches them, so stops and targets gather there.

qs.q: Roughly when is the Asian session in Pakistan time?
o: About 5 am to 12 pm
6 pm to midnight
12 pm to 5 pm
1 am to 4 am
qs.e: Read session times in real time, not broker server time; summer and winter differ by an hour.

qs.q: What is the London Judas swing?
o: London sweeping one Asian side, then taking the real direction
London closing and its profit taking
New York's first hour and the news move
The first day of the week and Monday's range
qs.e: Low Asian volume builds a narrow range with stops on both sides.

qs.q: H4 is bullish. Which side of the Asian range is London more likely to take first?
o: The Asian low
The Asian high
Both at once
Neither
qs.e: Still, don't trade a guess; let the sweep happen and look for a CHoCH.

qs.q: Price closes above PDH with a strong body and holds there. How do you treat it?
o: A break; next target may be PWH
A sweep; sell at once
Nothing happened; just wait
IDM; look for a POI below
qs.e: In a sweep the body comes back inside; here the price was accepted.

qs.q: What is a typical weekly liquidity pattern?
o: One side is taken early, then the week heads for the other
The same direction every day, Monday to Friday
All of it happens Friday; the rest is range
PDH and PDL are both taken every day
qs.e: PWH and PWL are the best targets for swing traders; Monday often builds a narrow range.

qs.q: What does the final line of the 10-minute morning routine look like?
o: Bias bullish; watch an Asian-low sweep; target PDH
Make 100 dollars today, whatever happens
We'll see what happens; no plan needed
Only sells today, because Gold rose yesterday
qs.e: One line with bias, sweep zone and target.

qs.q: Why is trading inside the Asian range a mistake?
o: That range often gets swept in London, taking the stops
Because the market is closed in Asia
Because the spread is zero
It is not a mistake
qs.e: The Asian range is liquidity for London.

qs.q: Gold: PDH 4,152, Asian range 4,128 to 4,136, H4 bullish. In London price hits 4,125.40 and M15 closes 4,129.10. What is the target?
qs.e: A sweep of the Asian low, an M5 bullish CHoCH, buy near 4,130, stop 4,124.40; RR about 1:3.6.

qs.q: How do you spot a sweep on the chart?
o: Wick beyond, body back inside, next candles reverse
A big body closes beyond and the next candles stay
Price never reaches the level and turns early
An empty gap between two candles past the level
qs.e: A sweep is also called a liquidity grab or stop hunt.

qs.q: Why is the move after a sweep often fast?
o: Liquidity is used up and the big player has a side
A big news release always lands then
The broker pushes the price back
It isn't fast; it is always slow
qs.e: The buy orders above were used up and the big sell is in, so price drops back quickly.

qs.q: What is the real confirmation of a break?
o: The level holds from the other side on retest
The break candle is green
The break candle has a long upper wick
RSI moves above 70
qs.e: If price closes back inside on the retest, the "break" was really a sweep.

qs.q: What is the first and most important question to tell a sweep from a break?
o: Where did it close?
What colour is the candle?
What time is it?
How big is the spread?
qs.e: Price beyond the level can look convincing on a forming candle, but the close decides.

qs.q: What does a break candle usually look like?
o: A big momentum body with a small wick
A long wick with a small body
An indecision candle
A doji
qs.e: A sweep candle's long wick shows price went there and was rejected.

qs.q: A candle closes above the level, but the next candle takes back the whole move and closes below. What is it?
o: A two-candle sweep
A confirmed breakout
A bullish BOS
Inducement
qs.e: Watch the next one or two candles even after a close; a big opposite engulfing candle means a sweep.

qs.q: Which candle decides a sweep or break of an H1 level?
o: The H1/H4 close; confirm on M15/M5
The M1 close; confirm on M1 too
The Daily close; confirm on Weekly
A tick chart; no confirmation needed
qs.e: A single H1 wick can look like a full break on M5; don't mix timeframes.

qs.q: Where is the stop in a sweep trade?
o: Below the sweep wick, with some room
Right next to the entry
Above the target
No stop is needed
qs.e: If price closes below that wick again, the sweep idea was wrong.

qs.q: When is the entry in a break trade?
o: On the retest, or LTF confirmation after it
At market right on the break candle
A limit below the level before the break
Never; breaks are always fake
qs.e: No entry on the break candle; let price come back to the level.

qs.q: Gold example: 6.5-dollar stop, 1,000-dollar account, 1% risk. What lot?
qs.e: 10 ÷ (6.5 × 100) ≈ 0.015; round down to keep risk within 1%.

qs.q: When should you not trade at all?
o: Big news, mid-range, or mixed answers
A clear sweep with an LTF CHoCH
A clean break and retest with the bias
A setup with the bias in a killzone
qs.e: When in doubt, no trade.

qs.q: What do most "breakouts" turn out to be at first?
o: Sweeps
Real breaks
FVGs
Ranges
qs.e: That is why break entries come on the retest and sweep entries after a lower timeframe CHoCH.

qs.q: What is the DOL (draw on liquidity)?
o: The next liquidity pool price most likely reaches
An indicator that predicts the next direction
The day's open where everything starts
A trendline that price keeps returning to
qs.e: The DOL tells you how far price may go; that is the target.

qs.q: What is ERL?
o: Liquidity outside the range: past swing highs/lows, PDH, PDL
FVGs and small pullbacks inside the range
A special order block that forms outside
The broker's spread at outside levels
qs.e: IRL is inside the range: FVGs, pullbacks, small internal highs and lows.

qs.q: What is the rule about IRL and ERL?
o: Often IRL to ERL, then back to IRL
Price always reaches ERL and stays
Price never touches IRL again
The two are not related at all
qs.e: The market keeps breathing between the two.

qs.q: The SSL below has just been swept. What is the next DOL often?
o: The BSL above
More SSL further down
The middle of the range
Nothing
qs.e: After one side's liquidity is taken, the opposite side often becomes the next draw.

qs.q: Why should the take profit not sit right on the DOL?
o: Price often turns at or just before it
The broker won't allow a TP on the DOL
The DOL always breaks, so go beyond it
Right on it is actually best
qs.e: Put the target slightly before the DOL.

qs.q: Why is the time after the DOL is taken the most dangerous?
o: The big player is exiting and price heads to IRL
The trend speeds up and stops get run
The market shuts for a while afterwards
It isn't dangerous; it is the best entry
qs.e: Take profit, and work out the next DOL before any new trade.

qs.q: If you cannot write your DOL in one line, what does it mean?
o: No plan, just a guess; not trading is a decision
All is fine; trade any direction
Raise the lot so profit comes faster
Open M1 and take any signal
qs.e: Example: bias bullish, DOL = PDH, possible entry from the H1 FVG on the way.

qs.q: Gold: H4 bullish, London swept the Asian low, PDH 4,152 not yet taken. Price hits 4,152.30 then falls back to the FVG at 4,140. Who got caught?
o: The trader who bought again after PDH was taken
The trader who bought the FVG at 4,133
The trader with a 4,150.50 target
Nobody
qs.e: A new trade in the same direction after the DOL is taken often gets caught in the pullback.

qs.q: Which is NOT one of the Phase 2 gate conditions?
o: Filling an order block scorecard
Marking liquidity pools and sweeps on any chart
Telling a sweep from a break with the five questions
Saying in one line which liquidity price is heading to next
qs.e: The POI scorecard belongs to Phase 3.

qs.q: What does POI mean?
o: Where we expect a reaction and seek an entry
The highest price level on the chart
An indicator that draws zones itself
The broker server where orders go
qs.e: Point of Interest: Phase 3 answers the question of where to enter.

qs.q: What is the definition of a bullish order block?
o: The last red candle before the BOS move up
Any big red candle on the chart
The first green candle after a strong move
The biggest green candle of the BOS move
qs.e: Three parts: the last opposite candle, a strong move (displacement) and a break of structure.

qs.q: Why does the big player buy again when price returns to the order block?
o: To defend the first position and fill the rest
Because the broker tells it to buy there
Because the spread is lowest in that zone
It doesn't; only retail buys there
qs.e: The order block is like the big player's shop where it bought stock.

qs.q: In a strong order block, below which level does price usually not close?
o: The 50% (mean threshold)
The top edge of the zone
The 100% Fibonacci
No level
qs.e: Always add the 50% line to the zone.

qs.q: What is the better way for a new trader to draw the zone?
o: Full-candle zone, entry on LTF confirmation
Body-only zone, with no confirmation
No zone needed; a single line is enough
Wick-only zone, leaving out the body
qs.e: The full candle misses fewer reactions; confirmation keeps the stop small.

qs.q: Which is NOT one of the five signs of a strong order block?
o: The zone has been touched again and again
A BOS
Displacement and an FVG
A liquidity sweep before it
qs.e: The others are being unmitigated and in the right location; each touch uses up the orders there.

qs.q: If fewer than how many of the five signs are present should you skip an order block?
o: Three
One
Trade only with all five
Signs are not needed
qs.e: The more signs, the stronger the POI.

qs.q: What is the difference between an aggressive and a conservative entry?
o: Aggressive: limit in advance; conservative: wait for a CHoCH
Aggressive: wait for a CHoCH; conservative: limit in advance
They are the same; only the lot differs
Aggressive has no SL; conservative has one
qs.e: Aggressive never misses the move but takes the full stop if the zone fails; conservative sometimes misses the move.

qs.q: Gold M15: order block 4,100 to 4,107, entry 4,107, stop 4,099. What lot at 2% risk on a 1,000-dollar account?
qs.e: Risk 20 dollars, stop 8 dollars: 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5, so 0.02 lot (rounded down).

qs.q: What happens if a body closes below the order block?
o: The idea is over; it often becomes a breaker
Buy more; price is cheaper now
Remove the SL; price will come back
Nothing changes; the zone is still fine
qs.e: Staying in the trade after the zone fails is a mistake (lesson 3.3).

qs.q: How many candles make an FVG?
o: Three
Two
One
Five
qs.e: Candle 1, the big displacement candle in the middle, and candle 3.

qs.q: Where is a bullish FVG?
o: Between candle 1's high and candle 3's low, when they don't touch
Between candle 1's low and candle 3's high
In the middle candle's body
Between two days
qs.e: Bearish FVG: between candle 1's low and candle 3's high.

qs.q: What is the CE of an FVG?
o: The exact middle of the gap, 50%
The top edge of the gap
The middle candle's close
An indicator
qs.e: In a strong FVG price often turns at the CE; a body close beyond it weakens the FVG.

qs.q: Which is a sign of a weak FVG?
o: It sits mid-range and no high or low broke
A big-bodied middle candle
It came with a BOS
It is not filled yet
qs.e: A strong FVG is with the bias, comes with a BOS and is a reasonable size.

qs.q: What is an IFVG?
o: An FVG closed through strongly that now works in reverse
Two FVGs stacked on top of each other
A tiny FVG that forms on M1
A big FVG formed on the Daily chart
qs.e: A close above a bearish FVG turns it into support (a bullish IFVG).

qs.q: Where is the better stop in an FVG trade?
o: Below the move's origin (OB or swing low)
Just under the FVG, a dollar away
At the CE, the FVG's 50%
Next to the entry, the tightest stop
qs.e: A stop just under the FVG is often hit.

qs.q: When an FVG and an order block sit together, what is a good approach?
o: Enter in the FVG with the stop behind the order block
Ignore both
Enter only below the order block
Sell above the FVG
qs.e: Price often fills the FVG first, then touches the order block and turns.

qs.q: Gold M5: candle 1 high 4,125, candle 3 low 4,132. What are the FVG and CE?
o: FVG 4,125 to 4,132, CE about 4,128.5
No FVG
qs.e: If an M5 body had closed below 4,125, the FVG would have failed and become a bearish IFVG.

qs.q: Must every FVG be filled?
o: No; many stay unfilled in strong trends
Yes, every FVG always fills completely
Only M1 FVGs have to be filled
Yes, and it must fill the same day
qs.e: Not every small gap is an FVG; only those with displacement and a structure break matter.

qs.q: What is a breaker block?
o: A failed OB, broken after a sweep, now working in reverse
An ordinary successful OB in the middle of a trend
A three-candle gap that forms on the break
The day's high that breaks in London
qs.e: In a bullish breaker the green-candle zone that built the high is now support.

qs.q: What is the correct sequence of a bullish breaker?
o: Low, high, lower low, high breaks, retest
High, low, higher low, low breaks, retest
Low, higher low, high, high breaks, retest
Low, high, higher high, low breaks, retest
qs.e: At the lower low retail sells thinking it is a breakout, and gets trapped.

qs.q: What is the real power of a breaker?
o: The sweep: cheap liquidity first, then trapped sellers
The zone's large size holding more orders
The green or red colour of the zone's candles
Forming in Asia while the market is quiet
qs.e: The trapped sellers' stops sit above and give price more fuel.

qs.q: When do you trade a breaker?
o: On the retest
On the MSS candle
During the sweep
Never
qs.e: At the break price is expensive and the stop is large.

qs.q: What is the main difference between an order block and a breaker?
o: OB: a zone that worked; breaker: one that failed and flipped
They are the same, only named differently
Breakers mid-trend, OBs at trend changes
OB after a sweep, breaker without one
qs.e: Breakers appear mostly at trend changes; order blocks mid-trend.

qs.q: A zone broke without a sweep (a higher low formed). What is it?
o: A mitigation block
A breaker block
A rejection block
A propulsion block
qs.e: Without a prior sweep it is not a breaker (lesson 3.4).

qs.q: A bullish breaker forms in H4 premium. What happens to it?
o: It often fails
It always works
It is the best setup
It makes no difference
qs.e: Check the higher timeframe; otherwise a small breaker may just be a pullback.

qs.q: Gold M15: Asian low 4,112, green zone 4,116 to 4,124, London sweeps to 4,104, then 4,124 breaks. Entry and stop?
o: Entry 4,128, stop 4,124
Entry 4,104, stop 4,100
Sell at 4,124
qs.e: Target the previous day's high at 4,142; 9 dollars risk for 22, about 1:2.4.

qs.q: What does to mitigate mean?
o: Cutting a loss: exiting a wrong position near entry
Raising the lot to recover the loss fast
Opening a new opposite trade at the same spot
Removing the stop and waiting for price
qs.e: Where they exit, their orders push price again; that zone is the mitigation block.

qs.q: In a bullish mitigation block, what is the last low before the high breaks?
o: A higher low; the previous low did not break
A lower low; the previous low was swept
An exactly equal low
There is no low
qs.e: A lower low means a breaker; a higher low means a mitigation block.

qs.q: Which usually gives the stronger reversal, a breaker or a mitigation block?
o: The breaker, because liquidity is taken first
Mitigation, because the low never breaks
Both have exactly equal strength
Neither gives a reversal
qs.e: A mitigation block often signals continuation or a slower reversal.

qs.q: Where is a bearish mitigation block most common?
o: Downtrends: lower high, low breaks, then the red zone
At an uptrend's top, after a higher high
In the middle of a range, both ways
Only at big news, inside the spike
qs.e: Price makes a lower high, breaks the low, then returns and drops from the red zone.

qs.q: Is a wick touching the high a break for a mitigation block?
o: No, a body close is needed
Yes, a wick is enough
Enough on H4 only
Enough for sells only
qs.e: Trusting a weak break is a mistake.

qs.q: If the green-candle zone is very large, what do you do?
o: Use the 50% or the top candle
The whole zone, with a bigger lot
Skip the zone entirely
The whole zone, without an SL
qs.e: A big zone means a big stop and a poor RR.

qs.q: Gold H1: high 4,138 (zone 4,130 to 4,138), higher low 4,124 (the previous low 4,118 held), then 4,138 breaks. What zone is it?
o: A bullish mitigation block
A bullish breaker block
A bearish order block
A bearish rejection block
qs.e: Entry 4,134, stop 4,127, target last week's high at 4,152; about 1:2.5.

qs.q: How does a bearish rejection block form?
o: A long wick above BSL; body top to wick tip
A long red body; open to close
A gap between two candles; wick to wick
A small wick under the high; low to high
qs.e: Price went up, took the liquidity, but was not allowed to stay.

qs.q: When does a rejection block fail?
o: When a body closes beyond the wick tip
When price first touches the zone
When the wick is longer than the body
Never; it always works
